coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For When You're
Running On Empty
coverDek: For the exhaustion that sleep doesn't fix - five prayers for the tank that's been on empty longer than you've let on.

points.hook: Lord, I kept pouring from a cup You never asked me to refill alone.
paragraphs: I told myself rest was something I'd get to once everyone else was taken care of. I didn't notice the cup was empty until my hands started shaking just holding it. Teach me that stewardship was never meant to include my own collapse.
points.verseText: “Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while.”

points.hook: I decree: the pace that's draining me does not get to decide my future.
paragraphs: I will not die proving I can carry what was never mine to carry alone. Every yoke that isn't His, I'm setting down right now. In Jesus' name, I take back my rest - this exhaustion does not get the final word.
points.verseText: “My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”

points.hook: Lord, my body has been keeping score longer than my mind would admit.
paragraphs: The tight shoulders, the shallow breathing, the headaches I keep explaining away - my body has been asking for permission to stop and I haven't been listening. Meet me in the actual ache, not just in the waiting room of it.
points.verseText: “For I have satiated the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrowful soul.”

points.hook: We're not letting you carry this one alone anymore.
paragraphs: Somebody in this family is running on fumes and calling it faithfulness. We see you, we're praying with you, and we're not waiting for the burnout to finish before we show up for you. Comfort yourselves together tonight - that starts with us.
points.verseText: “Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another.”

points.hook: Come here, child. You don't have to earn rest from Me.
paragraphs: I'm not tallying up what you got done today before I let you lay your head down. The way a mother gathers a tired child without asking what they accomplished - that's how I'm gathering you now. Just come, tired is the only qualification.
points.verseText: “As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you.”

cta.closingLine: If this spoke to you, let's stay connected.
